 Govt faces questions on incentives for flood relief volunteers as monsoon preparedness comes under scrutiny
 Dewan Rakyat to examine rescue readiness, disaster response assets and financial assistance for flood-hit communities
 Updated 1 hour ago · Published on 19 Nov 2026 9:01AM
 MP to seek the Home Minister's explanation on the number of documented and undocumented foreign nationals - November 19, 2026 
 THE government's plans to support non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and volunteers involved in flood relief operations, including possible financial incentives, will be among the key issues raised in the Dewan Rakyat today as Malaysia prepares for the Northeast Monsoon.
 Wan Razali Wan Nor (PN-Kuantan) will seek clarification from the Prime Minister on whether incentives will be extended to NGOs and volunteers assisting flood victims, alongside the government's readiness in deploying rescue personnel, assets and welfare assistance during the monsoon season.
 According to the Parliament's Order Paper, the questions will be raised during the Ministers' Question Time (MQT).
 The sitting will also examine broader policy issues, including transport decarbonisation, foreign worker management, national productivity and proposed legislation addressing racial, religious and royal (3R) sensitivities.
 Datuk Larry Sng Wei Shien (PBM-Julau) will ask the Science, Technology and Innovation Minister how hydrogen technology can complement electric vehicles (EVs) in accelerating the transition towards low-carbon transport.
 Mohd Misbahul Munir Masduki (PN-Parit Buntar) will seek the Agriculture and Food Security Minister's final position on Malaysia's participation in the International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV) 1991, compared with UPOV 1978, under the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP).
 During the oral question-and-answer session, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari (PH-Gombak) will ask the Investment, Trade and Industry Minister about cross-ministry initiatives to improve economic and workforce productivity nationwide.
 Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) will seek the Home Minister's explanation on the number of documented and undocumented foreign nationals, measures against worker exploitation, the use of invalid employment documents and crime rates involving foreigners.
 Datuk Ewon Benedick (PH-Penampang) will ask the National Unity Minister when the proposed National Harmony Act or new legislation addressing 3R issues will be tabled in Parliament and the challenges delaying its introduction.
 The Dewan Rakyat will subsequently resume committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027), scheduled to continue until Nov 26, before winding-up sessions by the Housing and Local Government Ministry and the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry. - November 19, 2026
